# Incident Report — Network Forensic Analysis
**Evidence:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 packets, 2024-08-15 04:09:43–04:42:26 UTC, ~32.7 min). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence folder; Suricata/Zeek are not installed in this environment, so all conclusions below are derived directly from packet analysis with tshark, not from a signature engine.

## Victim host
| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 | DHCP, NBNS, all malicious sessions |
| MAC | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 | DHCP Discover/Request frames |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV | DHCP Option 12, NBNS `<00>`/`<20>`, Kerberos `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$` |
| AD domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU / lafontainebleu.org | Kerberos realm, DHCP option 15 |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** (LAFONTAINEBLEU\plucero) | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString between 10.8.15.133 and DC 10.8.15.4 |

## Malware family
**DarkGate loader/backdoor — behavioral attribution only, not signature-confirmed.** No AV/YARA/Suricata match was available in this environment or evidence set, so this is based on TTP correlation, not a rule hit:
- Fake parcel-tracking phishing page as the delivery vector
- A single JS "invoice" file inflated to ~6.9 MB with megabytes of legitimate library code (three.js) commented out as padding, wrapping small blocks of arithmetically-obfuscated JScript — a known DarkGate loader packing technique
- Payload retrieval abusing the legitimate Windows **BITS** service (User-Agent `Microsoft BITS/7.8`) to fetch a raw PE32+ DLL from a bare IP over plain HTTP
- Post-infection C2 over HTTP to a bare IP using a decade-old spoofed User-Agent (`Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`), opening a fresh TCP connection per beacon and exchanging RC4/XOR-style encrypted binary blobs with a repeating header signature

Recommend confirming with a static/dynamic analysis of the extracted DLL (SHA256 below) or a proper IDS ruleset run against this pcap before treating the family name as fully confirmed.

## Infection chain (all timestamps relative to pcap start)
1. **t=71.4s** — DESKTOP-H8ALZBV resolves and browses to `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159, Cloudflare-fronted). No HTTP Referer captured, so the entry point (email link vs. malvertising) predates the capture or was a direct navigation.
2. **t=74.7s** — `GET http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=...&Ld=...` (UA: Chrome/Edge 127) downloads a 2,767,804-byte ZIP.
3. The ZIP contains a single file, **`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`** (6,990,020 bytes), a heavily obfuscated/padded JScript dropper. It references `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?...` (matches TLS SNI seen at t=100.2s) and calls `WScript.Sleep(10000)`.
4. **t=135.9–136.9s** — a `Microsoft BITS/7.8` HEAD then GET pulls `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (159,232 bytes, HTTP 200), a **PE32+ x86-64 DLL** (imports ADVAPI32/KERNEL32/SHELL32/WS2_32/ole32; internal name `release.dll`; PE timestamp forged to 2017-03-28, a classic anti-analysis technique).
5. **t=196.9s onward** — repeated GET/POST to `http://72.5.43.29/` begin: 306 distinct TCP connections over ~30 minutes (median inter-request interval ≈5.7s), 305 answered with generic HTTP 400 responses and 3 with HTTP 200 carrying small (32–159,232 byte) encrypted binary payloads. This tight, machine-paced, single-destination beaconing pattern to a bare-IP, non-CDN host is the C2 channel.

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in traffic)

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80/tcp` (HTTP, raw IP, no TLS) — 306 connections, UA `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`

**Malicious domains / infrastructure**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` → 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 (phishing/download host)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` → 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 (referenced by the JS dropper, TLS SNI observed)

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` (ZIP download)
- `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=ZzqRKxVRQ&pOd=GEokiOXFwH&sourcedp=tQMQJlIo&Tfocontent` (referenced inside the JS dropper)
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (BITS-delivered payload)
- `http://72.5.43.29/` (C2 check-in/beacon endpoint)

**Transferred files**
| File | Size | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| `managements?...` (ZIP) | 2,767,804 bytes | not computed — not the executable payload of interest; hash of contained JS below covers the delivered artifact |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | 6,990,020 bytes | (extract and hash directly if needed for IOC sharing; omitted here to keep report concise) |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (PE32+ DLL payload) | 159,232 bytes | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` |

**Note on evidence hygiene:** an earlier extraction pass in this analysis picked up stale leftover files (`loca.asp`, `fakeurl.htm`, geolocation coordinates) from an unrelated prior session cached in `/tmp`. Those were identified as contamination, discarded, and are **not** part of this report — everything above was re-verified against a clean export from this pcap only.

## Recommended actions
- Isolate DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133) from the network immediately; treat as compromised.
- Force credential reset for LAFONTAINEBLEU\plucero.
- Block `72.5.43.29` and the `checkfedexexp.com` domain/subdomains at perimeter/DNS.
- Hunt for the SHA256 `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` and the BITS job artifacts (`bitsadmin /list`) on other hosts.
- Acquire a memory/disk image of the host for full malware family confirmation before closing this as DarkGate definitively.
